links.l: Artemis I flight day 20: Orion conducts return powered flyby (NASA)

arrival.source: NASA Artemis I: outbound powered flyby 2022-11-21 about 80 miles above the lunar surface (flight day 5 blog); return powered flyby 2022-12-05, 80.6 miles above the surface (flight day 20 blog). The distant retrograde orbit between them is not drawn: the trajectory model has no such arrival type.

events.label: Launch — SLS Block 1 / Orion
events.description: Kennedy Space Center LC-39B, 2022-11-16, 06:47 UTC (1:47 a.m. EST). The first flight of the Space Launch System, with Orion uncrewed.

events.label: Moon — outbound powered flyby
events.description: 2022-11-21, closest approach at 7:57 a.m. EST (12:57 UTC), about 80 miles above the lunar surface after a 2 minute 30 second burn: the first of two maneuvers to enter a distant retrograde orbit.

events.label: Distant retrograde orbit insertion
events.description: 2022-11-25. Orion enters the distant retrograde orbit around the Moon.

events.label: Distant retrograde departure burn
events.description: 2022-12-01. A 1 minute 45 second burn of the main engine on the European Service Module, about 454 feet per second, takes Orion out of the orbit.

events.label: Return powered flyby
events.description: 2022-12-05, 80.6 miles above the lunar surface. A 3 minute 27 second burn of about 961 feet per second redirects Orion toward Earth.

events.label: Splashdown — Pacific Ocean
events.description: 2022-12-11, 12:40 p.m. EST (17:40 UTC), off the coast of San Diego, after 25 days 10 hours 53 minutes.
